notes: Runner clicked for 1 credit 4 times a turn on T3, T4, T13 and T14 while sitting on 12-28 credits with a full grip, and never ran Server 1 while Corp advanced Obokata Protocol (T6-T8, T11-T13) and the final Send a Message (T14-T15) behind a Loki that only asks for a grip shuffle. The T5 Into the Depths/Server 1 steal of Send a Message was good, and the T7-T10 R&D digs were defensible, but at T14 with 24 credits the Runner let the game-winning agenda through without a single run.

Solid aggressive MaxX game: Falsified Credentials to read Cyberdex Sandbox (T3), Black Orchestra from heap to steal it, then GFI (T5), R&D Cyberdex (T6) and Offworld Office (T9). Minor issues: the T2 Gachapon dig installed nothing and exiled three cards, and the T1/T8 runs into unrezzed ice with 1 credit were low-value facechecks.

After two Stimhack core damage cut max hand size to 3, the Runner spent T7-T12 drawing 2 cards and discarding 2 every turn while holding 18-26 credits and installing no breakers (Black Orchestra/Paperclip only arrived T14), letting Nisei MK II score twice from Server 3 (T10, T12). The game ended with a foreseeable flatline on T17: with 3 cards, Anansi (4 net) already revealed by Celebrity Gift and swapping around via Thimblerig, the Runner made a second run on Server 3 and Thimblerig swapped Anansi in front.

Won T10 with good use of Hippo on Gatekeeper (T6), Yusuf counters on Hagen/Vanilla, and Archives/HQ runs for the final 6 points. Weaknesses were cheap facechecks with 0-2 credits on T4 (Server 1, Vanilla) and T5 (Server 2 Hagen, R&D Gatekeeper), and Clone Chip being installed but never used.

The early game was decent (Mad Dash trash of Regolith T2, Engolo+Ika through Anansi to steal Obokata T8), but the T3 R&D facecheck into DNA Tracker cost 3 cards and 6 credits. On T11 the Runner spent 8 on Endurance, then ran a 4-ice remote with about 5 credits into Loki copying the known Anansi, chose to shuffle its grip to continue and was flatlined by the remaining net damage; a competent player would not run that server that turn, or would let the run end rather than shuffle away the grip.

Won T9 by hammering the open R&D and taking two Efficiency Committees from Archives, but the play was robotic: the Runner sat at exactly 7 credits and 3 unplayed cards for eight turns and never drew or installed a second piece. It also re-ran Server 1 to access the same Cybernetics Court five times (T7-T9) without trashing it, while Corp scored two Project Vitruvius from Server 2 unchallenged after one Gatekeeper bounce (T5).

Clean MaxX win on T9: Mad Dash plus Paperclip from heap stole Offworld Office (T6), then Offworld Office (T8) and GFI (T9) from the same remote, with Liberated Account and Daily Casts as economy. The only blemishes were breakerless facechecks into Magnet on HQ (T1) and R&D (T3).

The Runner never installed, played or drew a single card for 16 turns; from T4 it ran into the known Slot Machine on R&D four times a turn (and later two Slot Machines), sitting at 0 credits while Corp went past 100 credits. On T13-T14 it ran into IP Block eight times at 0 credits, gaining a tag each time. Obokata Protocol (T12) and two Nisei MK II (T14, T16) scored with no real contest; clicking for credits and installing breakers was the obvious alternative.

On T3 the Runner shuffled its whole grip into the stack to get past Loki and then jacked out without accessing. It then never ran Server 1 again although Loki was its only ice: GFI (T4-T5), Vitruvius (T6-T7) and two Megaprix Qualifiers scored there. On T8 and T9 it clicked for credits eight times at 19-27 credits while Corp sat one agenda from winning, rather than running Server 1 at the cost of a grip shuffle.

The mid-game was reasonable (Hippo+Black Orchestra through Magnet for Megaprix T7, Vitruvius from R&D T9), but from T10 to T15 the Runner clicked for 1 credit about 16 times while holding 5 unplayed cards and never drew toward a fracter for the Hagen/Loki ice. It also spent 9 credits per run on Fairchild 3.0. Corp's final GFI was installed and advanced in Server 2 on T15 and scored T16 without the Runner even attempting the server.

Won T15 against a Corp that never installed a single ice, but needed 15 turns because it usually made only one run per turn while spending clicks on Engolo, Aumakua, two Datasuckers, Boomerang and Hippo with nothing to break. It also used Zer0 every turn, throwing away Keiko, Sure Gamble, Engolo and Aumakua to net damage; with all servers open, three or four HQ/R&D runs per turn would have ended the game far sooner.

Against a Corp that only clicked for credits from T8 to T24, the Runner never ran R&D until T22 and kept making low-value Archives runs and credit clicks (T10, T20). It declined to steal Obokata Protocol from HQ on T13 and T19 although it had enough cards to pay the 4 net damage, and let Slot Machine drain it to 0-3 credits late. It finally won on T26 by taking the same Obokata it had passed on earlier.

The Runner ran the open R&D four times a turn for 12 turns and never once ran Server 1, a single-ice remote where Corp scored Vacheron (T3), The Future is Now (T5, T9), Hyperloop Extension (T7) and the winning Hyperloop (T20). It played no cards besides one Sure Gamble, clicked for credits up to 23, and on T19, with Corp at 6 points and a card advanced in Server 1, it trashed a Marilyn Campaign and clicked for credits instead of running the remote.

After spending 6 credits removing three Hard-Hitting News tags on T2, the Runner sat at 0 credits and ran into the known IP Block on Server 1 four times per turn on T3-T8 and T10, roughly 26 identical runs that each ended the run and added a tag. It never clicked for credits or played a card while Degree Mill (T6) and two Bellonas (T9, T11) scored from that server.

The Runner's economy never recovered: it held five unplayed cards all game, discarding to hand size every turn from Hoshiko draws, and spent clicks and 2 credits each removing tags on T7, T11 and T12 with no resources to protect. It facechecked Enigma on Server 1 with 2 credits (T8), got in on T9 but could not afford Bellona's steal cost, and was at 0-2 credits when Degree Mill was installed and scored (T13-T14) for the win.

Won only because Corp decked on T18. The Runner ran a 3-card HQ four times a turn on T2-T5, seeing Dedication Ceremony repeatedly, while Corp advanced and scored Efficiency Committee from Server 1 (T1-T3 and T6-T7) without a single remote run. From T11 to T17, needing one point, it spent about 28 runs re-accessing Hedge Fund, Biotic Labor and Archived Memories in HQ, feeding Architect free installs each time, and never played its 3 cards or used its 9 credits.

The T1 Stimhack facecheck into HQ with no breakers cost a core damage for nothing. The Runner then never ran Server 1 even once while Corp installed and advanced Nisei MK II (T5-T6), SSL Endorsement (T7-T8) and the winning Nisei (T11-T12) there. It spent those turns installing a second and third Liberated Account, Clone Chip, Hippo and D4v1d with 10-12 credits; a competent player would have pressured the remote on T5, T7 and T11.

The Runner clicked for credits four times a turn for most of 22 turns, piling up 55 credits while MaxX milled its own breakers. On T16 it hit Macrophage's traces 4/3/2/1 with 40 credits and paid 0 to raise link, losing every trace including the trace-1 end the run. It then went back to clicking for credits while Corp scored Cyberdex Sandbox (T17, T18), Offworld Office (T20) and GFI (T22) from Server 3, never contesting that server again.

Competent win on T19: stole Efficiency Committee through Architect (T5), used Hippo to clear Gatekeeper (T8), Vanilla and Hagen, and won with repeated HQ/R&D pressure plus Yusuf/Imp counters. Lapses were letting Project Vitruvius be installed (T10) and scored from Server 2 (T11) while spending T10 on Knobkierie and Yusuf installs, and an early Hagen facecheck on T2.

After two Hard-Hitting News the Runner removed only 2 of 8 tags (T2) and then sat at 0 credits with 6 tags from T3 to T9. It ran open R&D four times a turn and never clicked for credits or played the cards it kept discarding. Corp, building to 15 credits, flatlined it on T10 with High-Profile Target; staying heavily tagged and broke against a tag deck was a foreseeable loss.
